problems.problem: The previous misregistered center-anchored plate is fixed (the base contact crop [177,1156,903,1406] now shows the glass plinth resting on one continuous darker olive plate with no vertical seam and no stray top edge under the bottle; contact shadow opacity 0.35 / offset_y 0 reads as a tight soft darkening, no floating). But the plate rectangle (x=180,y=980,w=720,h=460) stops 180px short of both side margins, so its vertical edges print as two hard tabs floating in the open field beside the bottle's lower body, and its top edge y=980 reads as a short horizontal line at each side instead of the brief's full-width 'plate sunk behind the dot field'. The lower half still carries accidental geometry rather than a designed band.

The stipple narrative is only half delivered: the bone-white powder dots are legible at the top edge and thin downward, but the 'crisp hard-edge blank horizontal band from the lower third' is not a clean blank plaque - it is occupied by the offset darker rectangle and, outside it, by a second full-width tonal transition near y≈1120 visible left and right of the plate. The eye meets two competing horizontal edges in the settling zone, so 'dust落定 at a zero line' reads as print-layer mismatch compared with R1/R4's confident single-field control.

The ABOVE monument grid (logo / near-full-width Bodoni title / subtitle / powder rule, all ending well above the cap at y≈490) is well resolved, but the bottle's grounding moment sits exactly where the plate's top edge and side edges converge behind the contact line; the quiet blank band the brief reserves for the base is instead the busiest tonal zone of the poster. Half the canvas below y≈980 is organized by edges that neither center nor frame the product.

Concept elements exist (stipple fall, plaque band, olive plate, powder rule) but they do not yet act as one system: the plate's opacity 0.35 difference is too subtle to read as an intentional second ink layer at viewing distance, while its hard side edges are too loud to read as atmosphere. Against R4's luminous centered mass and R1's clean plaque hierarchy the field still looks under-art-directed rather than deliberately silkscreened.

changes.value: Seamless flat matte silkscreen-printed card in deep olive moss green, fine bone-white stipple powder dots dense along the top edge and thinning gradually downward through the upper half, one crisp hard-edge blank horizontal band with no dots beginning exactly at the lower third and running to the bottom edge, perfectly even shadowless frontal illumination, flat graphic ink light, no texture gradients beyond the printed dots, no objects, no seams, no vertical divisions, no horizontal lines except the single blank-band edge
